description: The image displays two pie charts comparing performance outcomes across different categories, likely from an experiment or analysis in the paper “Laying the Foundation First: Investigating the Generalization from Atomic Skills to Complex Reasoning Tasks.” The left pie chart, labeled “Atomic Skill Fail,” is divided into four segments: a large dark teal segment (68.0%), a light gray segment (12.0%), a medium teal segment (12.0%), and a white segment (8.0%). The right pie chart, labeled “Reason Error,” contains four segments as well: a large medium teal segment (55.0%), a light gray segment (21.0%), a white segment (14.0%), and a small dark teal segment (10.0%). A partial legend at the top indicates that dark teal corresponds to “Atomic Skill Fail,” medium teal to “Correct,” and light gray to “Reason Error,” though the white segment’s label is not explicitly defined in the visible legend. The charts visually contrast the distribution of error types or outcomes, with the “Atomic Skill Fail” chart dominated by one large category and the “Reason Error” chart showing a more balanced but still skewed distribution. Percentages are displayed directly on each slice, and no slice is exploded or emphasized beyond its proportional size.
